Team — forwarding Novus's questionnaire. Draft answers below (these are meant to be conservative but negotiable):

1) IP: Redwood proposes the standard approach: customer retains ownership of customer data; Redwood retains ownership of the platform and pre-existing models. We will grant customer a limited license to use model outputs as specified in the order form. We will not seek rights to customer data beyond necessary processing.

2) Indemnity: Redwood can offer a mutual indemnity for IP infringement claims (Redwood indemnifies Novus for Redwood-delivered software infringing third-party IP; Novus indemnifies Redwood for customer content). For third-party claims arising from customer data that violates law, we expect Novus to indemnify. We should avoid open-ended warranties.

3) Liability cap: propose cap equal to fees paid in the prior 12 months, with a minimum floor of $2,000,000 for enterprise deals. Carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and violations of data protection laws (e.g., willful violation of data residency obligations).

4) Order form: Redwood prefers USD, EOM-30 payment terms. Termination-for-convenience at 30 days is acceptable; Novus asked for 60 — recommend proposing 45 days as a compromise.

5) Insurance & audits: standard cyber liability (minimum $5M) — we can provide certs upon request; for audits we prefer questionnaire responses and SOC 2 report in lieu of intensive on-site audits.

Please review and flag any redlines. If you agree, I'll incorporate these answers into the spreadsheet and attach a draft order form with the liability cap language and Exhibit A (SLA/data residency options).

- Vanessa

Hi Sofia — attaching our completed questionnaire and a draft order form for your review. Key points summarized below so your legal team can triage quickly:

- IP: Customer retains all rights to their data. Redwood retains platform & model IP. We grant a limited license for output use. No transfer of customer IP.
- Indemnity: Mutual IP infringement indemnity; customer indemnifies for claims arising from customer content or data.
- Liability cap: Liability limited to the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (b) $2,000,000, except for liability resulting from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or violations of privacy/data residency obligations.
- Order form: Draft in USD, net 30. We proposed termination-for-convenience of 45 days (open to discuss).
- Insurance: Redwood carries cyber liability insurance with $10M limits; certificate available on request.

Attachments: Redwood_Novus_LegalQA_Answers.pdf (completed questionnaire), OrderForm_Draft_Redwood_v1.docx, Redwood-SLAs-ExhibitA.pdf (SLA & data residency options).

If Novus has mandatory regulatory exceptions (e.g., absolute prohibition on cross-border processing), call that out and we can propose an Exhibit (private deployment/VPC + dedicated capacity) and update pricing.

Looking forward to your team's feedback — happy to jump on a call with legal to walk through the items.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
